description: Definitions of hooks/ and scripts/ that look alike and are allowed to coexist because they answer different questions. Read by tests/defs_registry (python3 -m tests.defs_registry), which groups every literal definition by the sameness rule of tests/defs_registry/check.py and fails on a group the register does not split. Each entry: a reason (required) and two or more sides; the definitions of one side answer one question, so two copies on one side are still a duplicate. A definition is identified by its scope-qualified name and the fingerprint of its sorted members (sha256, 16 hex), never by file or line; `at` is where it was when registered. Seeded from the duplicate-definition audit of f199dfb1e: its 61 different-questions families (sides = the distinct member sets of the family) and its ruled-out look-alike pairs (sides = the named definitions).

ceiling.note: tests/defs_registry/test_defs_registry.py fails when this tree has more uncovered groups, or more definitions in them, than this; lower it as merges land, never raise it to admit a new copy. The goal is 0 and 0.

The two-member sets ask whether a redirection reads a file; the wider sets ask whether it feeds a stream or which fd a redirection names by default.

Two vocabularies of lib/shell_parse.py: word-part kinds (backtick, cmdsub, procsub_in, procsub_out) and walk contexts (cmdsub, backtick, procsub, top). pretool-grep-backtrack-guard.py:132 _SUBSTITUTIONS is a context list passed to walk(into=...), checked at :387.

The disk guard's _DG_FIND_WORDS is the whole find grammar it admits; the userintent rule's two sets are the words it skips before reading -exec and those of them that take a value; the runtime guard's _FIND_PREPATH_ARG_OPTS the depth options (find's and fd's) that may come before the start paths. Each is a different reading of find.

_PY_READER_MODULES are modules that, run with python -m, only read the files named; _PY_SAFE_MODULES are modules whose import in -c code loads no other code and runs nothing. A module can be either without the other (json.tool vs math).

entries.source: lane closetests, check group on the join of 2026-11-21
entries.reason: close_exit.CYCLE_COMMANDS asks which openers' hook-minted task id a /close typed with no task binds (close.md: the /dev cycle's or the /do task-id), so /do is in it; prompt-workflow._DEV_COMMANDS asks which commands the ordinary /dev start runs for (_ordinary_dev_start, the start subcommand), and /do has a start of its own; stop-command-gate.refused_step asks which commands' runs may end on a REFUSED: Step line, /close included. Adding /do to _DEV_COMMANDS would run the /dev start for /do; dropping it from CYCLE_COMMANDS would leave a /do cycle unbound at /close.

SORT_OUTPUT_OPTS asks which option of sort names the file sort writes; _sd_writes_output asks whether an option of a git command (git's -o or any abbreviation git accepts of --output) sends that command's output to a file. Two programs' output options spelled alike, read with different abbreviation rules.

entries.source: defs-tools lane, check group on integration edc54b6e7
entries.reason: runtime_guard's _mutation_targets_for_verb asks whether a chmod argument is a symbolic mode (+, - or = followed only by mode letters, so it is not a path the chmod changes); shell_parse's _attr_operands asks where the option words of chmod, chown, chattr and setfacl end and their path operands begin (a word led by -, + or = is an option or a chattr attribute change, not a path). One classifies a mode string, the other splits options from operands for four verbs; they share only the three sign characters.

entries.source: defs-tools lane, check group on integration edc54b6e7
entries.reason: harness_vocabulary.WRITE_TOOLS asks which tools write a file (the write gate's rules, tool-policy's role rows, the cp-state, config and switch guards), NotebookEdit included; spec_path.EDIT_TOOLS asks which tool calls name their target in tool_input.file_path: spec_path reads it to find the last write of a spec monolith (a markdown file, which NotebookEdit cannot write), report_provenance to find the main agent's previous file write, with NotebookEdit's notebook_path on a branch of its own. Different questions: adding NotebookEdit to EDIT_TOOLS would read file_path from a call that does not send it.

The git privilege guard asks which ref a git update-ref / symbolic-ref call moves, to judge a protected branch; the overnight policy shim asks the same of its own argv, but it is a bash script installed alone on the overnight PATH (verified with cmp) and cannot read a Python definition.

READING_PIPELINES asks which pipelines dispatch agents the gitignore preflight lets read their own obligation; subagentstop-codex-enforce asks which pipelines dispatch agents that are not bound by /dev --codex; stop-command-gate's no_owner_end asks which commands may end on a NO_OWNER line. All are close and commit today, but each is its own rule's scope.

Each regex finds a different thing whose name ends .py or .sh: tool-policy a hook entry file a command runs, check-enforcement-evidence the script word of a settings hook command, render-settings the scripts a file references, check-file-references.sh (a shell script, which cannot read a Python definition) a markdown reference to a script.

userintent asks which command words run the rest of their line as a command (source, ., exec, env); check-file-references.sh asks which shell words read a named file as code (source, ., exec), and is a shell script that cannot read a Python definition.
Both ask which CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS values mean off; session-info.sh is a shell SessionStart hook and cannot read the Python TASKS_OFF of stop-command-gate.py.

Both ask where the system git binary is. The overnight policy shim and the git selector are bash scripts, each installed alone as `git` in its own directory and verified with cmp (scripts/overnight-git-env.sh), so neither can source a file the other also reads.

diff-mutate.TARGET_ROOTS asks which directories mutation testing mutates; render-settings._CODE_DIRS asks which harness directories a hook command runs files from; scripts/install/land asks the same as render-settings of a settings overlay, but is a shell script and cannot read the Python definition.
